voice.airout.window: Here’s the best time to air out your home: {when}. That’s when the forecast shows the least smoke where you are. A forecast can be wrong, so if you see or smell smoke then, keep your windows closed.
voice.airout.now: The forecast shows little or no smoke where you are right now. So the best time to air out your home is now, if the smell is gone. If you still smell smoke, keep your windows closed.
voice.airout.none: For now, keep your windows closed. The forecast shows smoke where you are through the next {n} hours, with no real break. Check again later: the forecast is updated twice a day.
voice.airout.notAvailable: I couldn’t read the smoke forecast just now. That doesn’t mean the air is clear. You can check again in a little while.
voice.airout.notAvailable.replay: This is a replay of August 25, 2025. There’s no smoke forecast for that day: forecasts are kept for only about two days.
voice.airout.strip: Under the answer, a chart shows the smoke forecast hour by hour. Taller bars mean more smoke. A sun marks the day, and a moon the night.
voice.airout.source: The forecast comes from Environment and Climate Change Canada.
airout.label: Best time to air out your home
airout.title: {label}: {answer}
airout.now: Now, if the smell is gone
airout.shows.clear: The forecast shows no smoke here then.
airout.shows.light: The forecast shows the least smoke here then: a little, not none.
airout.shows.now.until: The forecast shows no smoke here until {when}.
airout.shows.now.until.light: The forecast shows only a little smoke here until {when}.
airout.shows.now.all: The forecast shows no smoke here for the next {n} hours.
airout.shows.now.all.light: The forecast shows only a little smoke here for the next {n} hours.
airout.caution: A forecast can be wrong. If you see or smell smoke then, keep windows closed.
airout.caution.now: Still smell smoke? Keep windows closed. A forecast can be wrong, and smoke from close by is not in it.
airout.none.body: The forecast shows smoke here through the next {n} hours, with no break of {min} hours or more.
airout.none.again: Check again later: the forecast is updated twice a day.
airout.notAvailable.body: The smoke forecast could not be read just now. That does not mean the air is clear.
airout.notAvailable.replay: This is a replay of Aug 25, 2025. Smoke forecasts are kept for about two days, so there is none for that day.
airout.strip.title: Smoke forecast, next {n} hours
airout.strip.aria: Chart: the smoke forecast for the next {n} hours, hour by hour. {title}.
airout.strip.by: A forecast, not a measurement: Environment and Climate Change Canada’s FireWork model.
airout.list.show: Show the forecast as a list
airout.level.top: smoke level {level} of {max} ({low} µg/m³ or more)
airout.list.numbers: The levels are the classes of ECCC’s own legend: fine particles from wildfire smoke in the air near the ground (PM2.5), in micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³). Under 1, ECCC’s map shows no smoke.
airout.rule: How the best time is chosen: the first {min} hours or more in a row with the least smoke in ECCC’s forecast. It is this app’s reading of the forecast, not advice from ECCC.
airout.advice: Once the air outside is better, Health Canada advises opening doors and windows to replace the air inside with fresh air.
airout.limits: The forecast only includes smoke from wildfires already detected. Smoke from a new fire or from close by is not in it. If you see flames or a smoke column, call 911.
airout.link.legend: ECCC’s legend for the smoke levels
